title: In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/operational-state.ts, bound the three rung-2 examination queries to a 24-hour
description:
In repos/development-vessel/src/resolvers/operational-state.ts, bound the three rung-2 examination queries to a 24-hour window so the rung can observe its own repair.

Find these three consecutive lines (each occurs exactly once in the file):
      count("SELECT count() FROM execution WHERE metadata.examination_examined != NONE GROUP ALL;"),
      count("SELECT math::sum(metadata.examination_examined) AS count FROM execution WHERE metadata.examination_examined != NONE GROUP ALL;"),
      count("SELECT math::sum(metadata.examination_unexamined) AS count FROM execution WHERE metadata.examination_examined != NONE GROUP ALL;"),

Replace them with these three lines:
      count("SELECT count() FROM execution WHERE metadata.examination_examined != NONE AND executed_at > time::now() - 24h GROUP ALL;"),
      count("SELECT math::sum(metadata.examination_examined) AS count FROM execution WHERE metadata.examination_examined != NONE AND executed_at > time::now() - 24h GROUP ALL;"),
      count("SELECT math::sum(metadata.examination_unexamined) AS count FROM execution WHERE metadata.examination_examined != NONE AND executed_at > time::now() - 24h GROUP ALL;"),

The only change is inserting" AND executed_at > time::now() - 24h" before" GROUP ALL;" in each of the three queries. Change nothing else, no other line, and no other file.

WHY. Rung 2 asks a present-tense question: "Does anything land unexamined?" It answers it with an unwindowed all-time math::sum(metadata.examination_unexamined) and holds only when that sum equals exactly 0. A sum over all history is monotone non-decreasing, so once any single execution records one unexamined file the rung reports broken permanently, no matter how the system behaves afterward. That has already happened: the sum went from 0 to 1 at 15:34:43 today, from one execution whose staged path had been truncated. After that first trip the rung reports the same value regardless of system state, so it has stopped being a measurement. The ladder can never read 7 of 7 by its own arithmetic. All three queries are windowed together rather than only the unexamined sum, because the rung also reports staged_examined and an examined_fraction derived from these numbers; windowing one and not the others would report a 24-hour numerator against an all-time denominator.

DECLARED CONFLICT. This change is proposed by the same operator whose work rung 2 grades, so it deserves scrutiny rather than deference. Two facts bound the risk. First, it cannot improve today's verdict: the windowed query was executed read-only against the live database before this dispatch and still returns unexamined = 1, examined = 365 over 24 hours, so rung 2 continues to report broken exactly as it does now. It can only clear roughly 24 hours after the truncation event, and only if no further unexamined file appears. Second, the underlying defect that produced the single unexamined file has already been repaired and deployed in gap-to-feature.ts, so what the windowed rung will measure tomorrow is whether that repair actually held. A change that cannot flatter the party proposing it today, and that can only report clean after a full window of genuinely clean behavior, is an instrument repair rather than a weakened threshold. The holds condition stays exactly as it is: the sum must still be zero.

Rung 3 is deliberately left alone. Its covered_fraction is also all-time but it is rising on its own, from 0.3606 to 0.4199 across today, so it can still observe repair and needs no intervention. Only rung 2 is permanently pinned.
